findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify a PER-CHECK red/green signal for the run-history threshold (e.g. query the drift step's own prior output, or persist a per-check conclusion), since reconcile-bridge-canary.yml's run conclusion is set only by the heartbeat 'Fail job on stale' step and does not encode binding-drift redness.
evidence: Plan: 'the filer queries the same workflow's previous completed run conclusion ... previous-also-red => threshold met'
Plan applies the N>=2 threshold to 'the new CI-red filer, heartbeat, binding-drift'
reconcile-bridge-canary.yml:244-248 'Fail job on stale' is the ONLY failing step, guarded on steps.check.outputs.stale == 'true'
No workflow step fails the run on DRIFT_FOUND=true (binding-drift lifecycle step at :193-202 does not exit non-zero) — so a run with unhealed drift but no staleness completes GREEN
findings.finding: The consecutive-red threshold for the binding-drift filer is keyed to the workflow's previous completed RUN CONCLUSION, but the canary workflow's run conclusion is set red only by the heartbeat 'Fail job on stale' step (line 244); the binding-drift oracle never fails the run, so the run conclusion carries no per-check red/green signal for drift.
findings.location: Approach — 'CONSECUTIVE-RED STATE STORE' / Scope: canary/heartbeat/binding-drift filer
scenarios: Cycle 1: drift present, heartbeat healthy -> workflow concludes SUCCESS; Cycle 2: drift still present -> previous-run-conclusion query returns success -> threshold reads 'first red' forever -> binding-drift bug NEVER files despite consecutive drift
Or: heartbeat stale (unrelated) reddens the workflow, causing the binding-drift threshold to spuriously read 'previous-also-red'
findings.suggested_fix: For each cyclic check, derive 'previous red' from that check's OWN prior signal — e.g. the presence of an open tagged ticket plus a per-check prior-run marker, or query the specific step conclusion — rather than the whole-workflow run conclusion, which conflates heartbeat and binding-drift and is green while drift persists.

Directive shape assembled upstream in `_apply_inbound_conflict` (result.payload['pending_bug_ticket'] with title/description/parent_id/local_id/jira_key, asserted at test_conflict_filing_deferred.py:139-144) is where the new dedup tag + detected_by fields must originate — not named in Scope

The `pending_bug_ticket` directive built by `_apply_inbound_conflict` must carry the conflict-identity tag (local id + jira key) and detected_by; because that assembly site is not in the inventory, the dedup tag can be added to the filer but never populated from the conflict, shipping hollow/untagged tickets

Specify the new signature/directive fields (conflict-identity dedup tag from local id + jira key, detected_by) and update each stub double accordingly.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify and unit-test the has-tag dedup-search failure arm (fail toward not-filing + loud log, consistent with the run-history arm).
evidence: 'previous-run query failure => treated as first red (fail toward not filing, loud log)' is specified
No corresponding failure behavior for the has-tag dedup search, which gates the accumulate-vs-new decision
findings.finding: Only the run-history query failure arm is specified (treat as first red, don't file). The dedup has-tag search — which the plan says 'runs FIRST' — has no failure arm: if the has-tag search errors, it is unspecified whether the filer files (risking a duplicate) or aborts.
scenarios: Transient rebar/search outage during the */20 cron: filer can't confirm an existing open ticket and may open a second, defeating the anti-duplicate goal
findings.suggested_fix: State that a failed/ambiguous dedup search aborts filing with a loud log rather than opening a new ticket, and add a test for it.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a live/integration acceptance criterion that at least one filer invokes the real `rebar create` (and asserts exit code / well-formed ticket) against the documented contract, so create-arg/gate drift is caught rather than mocked past.
evidence: Context: 'silently break when create args/gates change (0e15/376d class: gate changes broke automated surfaces)'
Testing lists 'one ticket with template fields', 'abort with loud log' etc. — all describable via mocked create; no criterion exercises the real rebar create/exit-code boundary
Approach promises documenting 'exact rebar create args, exit codes ... so auto-filers always fire a well-formed create' but no test validates the real args against the live rebar create contract
findings.finding: The motivating failure class (0e15/376d: create-arg/gate changes silently broke automated create sites) cannot be caught by the planned tests, which exercise the create only through unit-level mocks — no test actually invokes a real `rebar create` with the documented args. The exact defect the plan targets (a create call that no longer fires well-formed after gate/arg drift) would slip through a green suite.
findings.location: Testing section + Acceptance Criteria (contract 'so auto-filers always fire a well-formed create')
scenarios: A future gate/arg change to `rebar create` (the exact 0e15/376d class) leaves every filer's mocked test green while the live create no-ops or errors in CI
findings.suggested_fix: Add an integration test (or CI smoke) that runs the actual filer create command end-to-end against a real rebar store and asserts a well-formed ticket + exit 0, tied to the contract doc's stated args.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add an explicit dependency edge (or [rebar:<child>] citation) to the detected-by child and quote the REBAR_DETECTED_BY contract the filers rely on.
evidence: 'detected_by stamped by all automated filers (env var from the detected-by child).'
No depends_on/[rebar:<C>] citation is present for the child that defines REBAR_DETECTED_BY
findings.finding: AC-5 and the detected_by additions depend on REBAR_DETECTED_BY 'from the detected-by child' but the plan does not cite a dependency edge to that child ticket, so the env var's provenance is an uncited cross-ticket reference.
findings.location: Acceptance Criteria line 5; Approach 'REBAR_DETECTED_BY env var'
scenarios: The detected-by child slips or defines the var differently; the filers stamp nothing or a wrong value and AC-5 cannot be proven in-session
findings.suggested_fix: Record depends_on the detected-by child and pin the exact env var name/format the filers read, or inline a fallback default if the child is absent.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify how the has-tag -> create sequence is made race-safe (e.g. re-query has-tag immediately before create and abort if now-present, workflow concurrency group, or idempotent create keyed on the stable tag) so overlapping runs cannot both file for the same check tag.
evidence: Plan: 'Dedup search runs FIRST: an existing open tagged ticket always takes the accumulate-comment path'
Plan asserts 'the */20 cron cannot spam' only for the accumulation-comment path (via the <24h marker check), not for the create path
No lock/CAS/atomic create-if-absent is described for the has-tag -> create sequence; two concurrent filers pass the has-tag gate before either creates
findings.finding: The consecutive-red CREATE path is a check-then-act with no atomicity guard: dedup search (has-tag) runs first and files only if no open tagged ticket exists, but concurrent runs of the same workflow (GitHub Actions can execute overlapping runs) can both observe an empty has-tag result and both create a ticket for the same check tag, producing the duplicate the plan exists to prevent.
findings.location: Approach — 'Dedup search runs FIRST' / 'the ticket store IS the durable state; no new store'
scenarios: Two overlapping workflow runs (retry, concurrent triggers, or a slow run overlapping the next */20 tick) both find no open tagged ticket and each file one bug for the same check => duplicate tickets
findings.suggested_fix: Add a GitHub Actions concurrency group per filer workflow (serializing runs) and/or a re-check of has-tag immediately before create; document the chosen mechanism in the contract doc.

findings.finding: The 'max one accumulation comment/day' rule needs durable state to know whether a comment was already posted today, but the plan explicitly forbids a new state store — the provenance/computation of the daily-comment dedup is unspecified.
findings.location: Approach: 'max one accumulation comment/day' + 'no new state store'
findings.suggested_fix: State that the filer lists the ticket's existing comments and suppresses a new accumulation comment when one already carries today's date, reusing GitHub's comment history as the durable state.

findings.finding: The plan asserts a FOUR-site audit surface including a distinct 'canary red-transition filer', but the two cited canary_bridge.py locations (~:226, :374) map to the heartbeat-alert and binding-drift-alert filers respectively; no 'canary red-transition filer' create-bug site exists at those lines, elsewhere in canary_bridge.py (only cmd_heartbeat_alert and cmd_binding_drift_alert call `create bug`), or in reconcile-bridge-canary.yml.
findings.location: Context/Problem: 'The audit surface is FOUR sites... the canary red-transition filer and the heartbeat filer (scripts/canary_bridge.py ~:226/:374)'
findings.suggested_fix: Either cite the actual red-transition create-bug site (file+line) if one exists in a workflow/script not yet inspected, or restate the surface as: heartbeat-alert (canary_bridge.py:226), binding-drift-alert (:374), and the conflict filer (applier.py:135) — and drop or re-scope the separate 'canary red-transition filer' row.

findings.finding: The plan's target recovery pattern ('recovery comment on green; close left to agents') conflicts with the actual behavior of two of the sites it audits: both the heartbeat and binding-drift filers ALREADY auto-close their alert ticket on green via `rebar transition open closed --force-close`. The plan neither acknowledges this existing auto-close nor states whether it is intentionally removing it.
findings.location: Approach: 'recovery comment on green; close left to agents'
findings.suggested_fix: Add a note in Approach/Scope that the two canary filers currently auto-close on recovery (per ticket 0e15) and specify the intended end state — keep auto-close, or replace with comment-only — then extend the Testing section's green-with-open-ticket case to assert the chosen transition/no-transition behavior.

findings.finding: The 'max one accumulation comment/day' element has no derivation source under the stated 'no new state store' constraint — workflow run history records conclusions/timestamps, not whether a comment was already posted today; with the */20 cron the accumulate path fires every 20 minutes.
findings.location: Approach — 'max one accumulation comment/day' + 'no new state store — the workflow's own run history is the durable state'
findings.suggested_fix: Derive the cap from the ticket itself: query the open tagged ticket's comments and post only if no accumulation comment carries a timestamp within the last 24h. This keeps 'no new state store' true (state lives on the ticket).

findings.finding: The consecutive-red run-history query (`gh api repos/{repo}/actions/workflows/{file}/runs`) requires the repo and the workflow-file identity as inputs, but the consuming workflow (.github/workflows/reconcile-bridge-canary.yml) currently only passes STALE/RUN_URL/DRIFT_* env vars to the script and is not enumerated as needing new inputs threaded through for each cycle site (heartbeat, binding-drift, canary red-transition).
findings.location: Approach — 'CONSECUTIVE-RED STATE STORE' clause; Scope bullet 'canary/heartbeat/binding-drift filer scripts or workflow logic'
findings.suggested_fix: Add a Scope sub-item naming reconcile-bridge-canary.yml and the specific new env vars (e.g. WORKFLOW_FILE, GH_REPO) each alert-lifecycle step must export for the run-history query, per cycle site.
